workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§146–148
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§146–148: Qada'an's Cry, Jebe's Arrow, and the End of the Taichi'ud
part: §§146–148 — Qada'an's Cry, Jebe's Arrow, and the End of the Taichi'ud
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§146–148, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Three sections. §146: after a night in which the Taichi'ud troops scatter, Chinggis Qahan rides to turn the fugitives back, hears a woman in a red robe on a pass crying out his name, and finds Qada'an, daughter of Sorqan-Shira, whose husband has been killed by Chinggis's own soldiers; next day Sorqan-Shira and Jebe, two men of Tödöge's Taichi'ud household, come in, and Sorqan-Shira explains why he was late. §147: Jebe admits that it was he who shot the collarbone of Chinggis's white-mouthed bay at Köiten, and vows to serve; Chinggis praises candour, gives him the name Jebe and orders him to his side. §148: Chinggis plunders the Taichi'ud, kills their noble houses down to the children's children, and winters at Qubaqaja. Several quotations are cut at natural pauses into units, and the note says where; Sorqan-Shira's explanation and Jebe's vow rest heavily on the Ming glosses, and the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Üdür gein baraγ̇asu situldužu qonoγsad čeriġüd süni böġed butaražuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: to end, be finished (as an auxiliary: 'when done') [了呵]
to oppose, stand against (stem inferred) [相抗着]
to stay the night, camp [宿來的(每)]
past participle, plural: those who had …

sentences.l: Day dawning-when, opposing, the camped soldiers, by night, then, scattered-is.
sentences.i: When day broke, the soldiers who had camped in opposition had scattered in the night.
sentences.n: Read this opening as one clause: 'day dawning-when' (üdür gein baraγasu, Ming 日明了呵), then the soldiers (čeriġüd, 軍每) who had camped 'in opposition' (situldužu, 相抗着), then butaražuγui 'scattered'. The ending -žu-γui is the pattern ködölžüġüi of the earlier parts: converb plus a contracted bui 'is'. baraγasu is bara- 'to end' plus the conditional -γasu, which the Ming renders 呵 'when'. gein is only 明 'bright'; I read it as 'dawning'. The Ming does not say whose soldiers they are; I take them to be the Taichi'ud troops left over from the battle at the Onon (§§144–145).

sentences.t: Küreġelegsed irgen küṅgen ülü čidaqun keġen

words.reading: 古舌列額列克薛惕 Küreġelegsed

morph.gloss: to camp in a ring, encamp [下營來每的]
past participle, plural: those who had …
to flee out, escape (stem uncertain) [逃出]

sentences.l: Camping-ring-ones, people, fleeing-out not able, saying,
sentences.i: The people who had made camp, saying they could not get away,
sentences.n: Küreġelegsed is küreġele- 'to camp in a ring' (Ming 下營) with -gsed, the plural past participle ('those who had …'); this is the recurring -γsan/-gsed pattern. ülü čidaqun is 'not able' (ülü with a non-past form, the Ming 不能). küṅgen 逃出 'fleeing out' is a form I cannot parse with certainty; I take it as a converb. The unit hangs on keġen 'saying', continued in the next unit.

words.reading: 古舌列額列克薛惕 Küreġeleġsed

morph.gloss: to camp in a ring, encamp [下營來每的]
past participle, plural: those who had …

sentences.l: Camping-ring-ones, from the place, not, moving-was.
sentences.i: did not stir from where they were.
sentences.n: Note ese against ülü in the unit above: ese 不曾 goes with a past verb ('did not'), ülü 不 with a non-past one ('cannot'). γažar-ača is 'from the place' (ablative -ača, Ming 地行). ködölžüġüi is the familiar 'moving-is'. Küreġeleġsed here is the same word as in the unit above, spelled with ġ.

morph.gloss: to be routed, flee in fear [走了的(每)]
past participle, plural: those who had …
to drive back, make turn back [敎退咱]

sentences.l: Fled-ones, people (acc.), let-us-drive-back, saying,
sentences.i: 'Let us drive back the people who have fled,' he said,
sentences.n: dürbegsed (走了的) is the plural past participle 'those who fled in fear'; ulus-i is the accusative. ičuγaja is ičuγa- 'to drive back' plus -ja, the Ming's 咱 'let us'. The speaker is not named here; the next unit supplies Chinggis Qahan. I take keġen as the converb 'saying'.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan qonoγsan γažar-ača morilažu dürbekün irgen-i ičuγ̇an

morph.gloss: to stay the night, camp [宿來的]
to be routed, rush in fear [忙走的]
participle in -kün (its force is uncertain; here read as 'hurrying')
to drive back, make turn back [敎退囘]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, from the camped place, horse-riding, rushing, people (acc.) turning-back,
sentences.i: and Chinggis Qahan mounted and, from the place where he had camped, hurried to turn the people back,
sentences.n: morilažu is mori 'horse' + -la- 'use, ride' + -žu (Ming 上馬着 'mounting'): a converb. dürbekün (忙走的) is a participle of the same verb as dürbegsed; the Ming 'hastily going' suggests the sense 'rushing'. ičuγan is the same ičuγa- as before, now with the converb -n. The sentence runs on into the next unit. γažar-ača keeps its ablative force here: he sets out from the camping-place (the Ming 行 on this word is only its stock gloss).

sentences.t: jabuqui-dur dabaγ̇an deġere nigen hulaγ̇an deġeltü eme küġün
sentences.l: Going-when, a pass on, one red robe-having woman,
sentences.i: As he rode, on a pass there was a woman in a red robe,
sentences.n: jabuqui-dur: jabu- 'go' + participle -qui + -dur, 'when going' (Ming 行時). deġeltü is deġel 'robe' + -tü 'having' (Ming 衣有的): the possessive -tü pattern, 'robe-having'. eme küġün is 'woman' (eme, Ming 婦) written with küġün 'person' (人): the two glosses are one noun, the Ming splitting it.

sentences.t: Temüžin že keġen jeke daγ̇u-γ̇ar qailan uilan baiqu-ji

morph.gloss: particle (Ming 也者); here marks the shouted name, elsewhere emphasis [(也者︀)]
to call out, cry out [叫喚]
accusative (after a vowel; here on a participle, glossed 行)

sentences.l: 'Temüžin, že!' saying, a great voice-with, calling-out, weeping, standing.
sentences.i: crying 'Temüjin!' in a great voice, calling out and weeping as she stood.
sentences.n: že after the name is the Ming's 也者, apparently a call-particle (compare its use elsewhere as emphasis). daγu-γar is 'with a voice' (instrumental -γar). qailan uilan are two converbs in -n, 'calling out, weeping'. baiqu-ji: bai- 'stand' + -qu + -ji; the Ming gives 行 (a dative or accusative sign) and I take it as 'as she stood'. Her name for him here is his old name, Temüjin, not Chinggis.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan öġesün sonosču jaγ̇un küġün-(n)ü eme tein qailan bijü keġen asaγ̇ura küġün ilebe.

morph.gloss: one's own, himself (Ming 自己; form unclear) [自己]
thus, so, in that way [那般]
to call out, cry out [叫喚]
converb used as a finite verb: is
converb of purpose: in order to …

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, himself hearing, 'What person's woman thus calling-out is?' saying, a man sent-to-ask.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan heard it himself and said, 'Whose wife is it that cries out like that?' and sent a man to ask.
sentences.n: öġesün 自己 'self' is unclear to me; I take it as 'he himself', that is, he heard her calling his name. jaγun küġün-(n)ü eme is 'what person's woman' (Ming 甚人的婦人), a genitive before its noun. tein … bijü: 'thus … is'. asaγura is asaγ- 'ask' + -ura, the converb of purpose, 'in order to ask' (as in abura 'in order to take'); the Ming 敎問去 'have (him) ask, go' supplies the sending; ilebe 'sent' (敎去了). Chinggis does not go himself yet; he sends a man.

sentences.l: That man going, asking-when,
sentences.i: The man went, and when he asked,
sentences.n: Plain converb chain: odču 'going', asaγbasu 'asking-when' (asaγ- plus the conditional -basu, Ming 問呵). The conditional here simply opens the answer in the next unit.

sentences.l: That woman, saying:
sentences.i: the woman said:
sentences.n: ügülerün is ügüle- 'to speak' + -rün, the converb that introduces speech; Shiratori ends it with a colon, and the quotation follows.

words.reading: 鎖舌兒中罕-失舌剌-因 Sorγan-Šira-jin

morph.gloss: Sorqan-Shira, a man's name [人名 的]

sentences.l: "Sorγan-Šira's daughter I; Qadaγ̇an name-having."
sentences.i: "I am the daughter of Sorqan-Shira, and my name is Qada'an."
sentences.n: Sorγan-Šira-jin ökin: the genitive -jin (after a vowel) before the noun, 'of-Sorqan-Shira daughter'. neretei is nere 'name' + -tei, 'name-having' (Ming 名字有的): the possessive -tei pattern. No copula is written; the sentence is two noun phrases with bi 'I'.

sentences.t: Ere-ji min-u ende čeri- ġüd barižu alan bijü.

morph.gloss: soldier, army (first half of čeri-ġüd, split across a line) [軍]
plural (second half of čeri-ġüd; the linking vowel -ü- is Shiratori's) [每]
converb used as a finite verb: is

sentences.l: Husband (acc.) my, here, soldiers seizing, killing is.
sentences.i: My husband has been seized here and killed by the soldiers.
sentences.n: Ere-ji is ere 'man, husband' with -ji, the accusative after a vowel; the Ming 行 marks it. So 'my husband (object)' and the soldiers are the actors: čeri- + ġüd, one word split across two printed words (Ming 軍 + 每). barižu 'seizing', alan 'killing' (both converbs) and bijü 'is'. English passive for readability.

sentences.t: Ere-jüġen alaγdarun Temüžin-i ere-ji min-u aburatuγai keġen unšižu

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name [(人)名 行]
accusative (here probably the doer; see note)

sentences.l: Husband-own being-killed-when, Temüžin (acc.), husband (acc.) my let-him-save, saying, calling-aloud,
sentences.i: When my husband was being killed, I called aloud, 'May Temüjin save my husband!'
sentences.n: Ere-jüġen has the reflexive-possessive -jüġen (after a vowel), 'her own husband' (自的). alaγdarun is ala- 'kill' + the passive -γda- + -run (Ming 被殺時). aburatuγai is the optative: abura- 'save' + -tuγai, 'let him save' (Ming 敎救). Temüžin-i carries the accusative sign, which is odd for the one who is to do the saving; the Ming glosses it 行 and I take it as a plain address or a looser use of -i. Another reading takes Temüžin-i as the object of unšižu, 'calling to Temüjin: let him save my husband'; the sense is nearly the same. unšižu is unši-, elsewhere 'to read, recite'; the Ming has 叫着 'calling'.

morph.gloss: to call out, cry out [喚着]

sentences.l: Crying-out, wept I, said.
sentences.i: I cried out and wept,' she said.
sentences.n: qailažu (converb) uilaba (past 'wept') bi 'I' keġebe 'said'. Shiratori closes the quotation after bi. The speech began at 'Sorqan-Shira's daughter'. Note how the one speech is cut at natural pauses into several units.

sentences.l: That man came.
sentences.i: The man came back.
sentences.n: irežü is the converb -žü used as a finite 'came' at the full stop (Ming 來着); the Ming's 着 marks it as a converb, so the finite sense comes from the full stop and the context.

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan to, this word telling-when,
sentences.i: When he told Chinggis Qahan what she had said,
sentences.n: Qaγan-a: dative-locative, 'to the Qahan' (Ming 皇帝行). ene üge 'this word' (這言語). üġüleġešü is üġüle- 'to tell' + -ġešü, the conditional (Ming 說呵, 'when told').

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ene üge sonosuγ̇ad qataražu kürčü
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, this word having heard, galloping, arrived,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, hearing it, galloped and arrived
sentences.n: sonosuγad: sonos- 'hear' + -uγad, the completed converb ('having heard'). qataražu glosses 點着 (a Chinese 'counting, checking'), which does not translate; I read qatara- as 'to gallop', an inference from the sense of the whole unit and one I am unsure of. kürčü 'arrived'.

morph.gloss: Qada'an, a woman's name [女名 行]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, at Qadaγ̇an, dismounting, met-one-another.
sentences.i: and, dismounting by Qada'an, they met one another.
sentences.n: Qadaγan-dur: dative-locative, 'at Qada'an'. baγužu 'alighting' (下着). teberildübe: the Ming 相見了 means 'met each other'; the reciprocal -ildü- is clear, and the root teber- may mean 'embrace', but I render only what the Ming gives.

sentences.t: Ere-ji in-ü bidan-u čeriġüd urida alažuγ̇ui

morph.gloss: his, her (genitive stem of the third person) [他的]

sentences.l: Her husband (acc.), ours soldiers, before, had-killed.
sentences.i: Her husband had been killed earlier by our own soldiers.
sentences.n: in-ü 'his, her' (他的) and bidan-u 'our' (咱的, the inclusive 'we') are genitive stems; čeriġüd urida alažuγui is 'soldiers beforehand had killed' (urida 先, with -γui 'was'). The unit is Shiratori's sentence; the point is that the army is Chinggis's own. Again Ere-ji carries the accusative.

sentences.t: Tede irge ičuγaγ̇ad Čiṅgis Qaγan jeke čerig mün tende baγ̇užu qonoba.

morph.gloss: the very, the same (Ming 只) [只]
to stay the night, camp [宿了]

sentences.l: Those people turned-back-having, Čiṅgis Qaγan, a great army just there dismounting, camped.
sentences.i: Having turned those people back, Chinggis Qahan dismounted with his great army on that very spot and camped.
sentences.n: tede irge ičuγaγad: 'those people having been driven back' (completed converb -γad). jeke čerig mün tende: 'great army, just there' (mün is the Ming's 只, 'the very'). baγužu qonoba: 'dismounting, camped'. The converb chain ends at the full stop.

morph.gloss: Qada'an, a woman's name [(女)名 行]
side by side, together (Ming 並; form unclear) [並]

sentences.l: Qadaγ̇an (acc.), summoning, having-her-come, side by side seated.
sentences.i: He had Qada'an called and brought, and seated her beside him.
sentences.n: ireġülžü is ire- 'come' + the causative -ġül- (Ming 敎來着). saγulba is saγu- 'sit' + causative -l-, but the Ming gives only 坐了 'sat'; I render 'seated her', since the verb is causative. dergečen 並 is 'side by side', but I cannot analyse the ending.

sentences.t: manaγarši üdür Sorγan-Šira, Žebe qojar Taičiγ̇ud-un Tödöge-jin haran aγsad tede qojar ber irebe kü.

words.reading: 鎖舌兒中罕-失舌剌 Sorγan-Šira

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who were

sentences.l: Tomorrow day, Sorγan-Šira, Žebe, two, Taičiγ̇ud's Tödöge's household-ones being, those two also came, indeed.
sentences.i: The next day Sorqan-Shira and Jebe, the two men who had been in the household of Tödöge of the Taichi'ud, also came.
sentences.n: manaγarši üdür is 'on the morrow' (Ming 明日); manaγar is 'tomorrow', the ending -ši is not clear to me. qojar 'two' stands after the two names, and again after tede 'those'. Taičiγud-un Tödöge-jin haran: two genitives before haran 'household people' (Ming 家人): 'Taichi'ud's Tödöge's household'. aγsad is a- 'be' + the plural participle, 'those who were'. ber … kü: 'also … indeed'.

words.reading: 鎖舌兒中罕-失舌剌-冝 Sorγan-Šira-ji

morph.gloss: Sorqan-Shira, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, Sorγan-Šira (acc.), saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spoke to Sorqan-Shira:
sentences.n: Ming 行 on Sorqan-Shira marks the one addressed. ügülerün as before, then the colon.

morph.gloss: adjectival locative: that which is on …
to throw down, cast off [撇下的]

sentences.l: "Neck-on's heavy wood (acc.), onto the ground, you who had cast down,
sentences.i: "You who threw the heavy wood on the neck down to the ground,
sentences.n: The speech is one long address built on participles, broken into three units. güžügün-deki: güžügün 'neck' + -deki, 'that which is on'; the Ming 項頸行的 'on the neck'. kündü mudun-i is 'heavy wood (acc.)', the Ming's way of saying the cangue (see the next unit). oγoγuluγsan: oγo- 'throw down' + causative -γul- + -γsan (Ming 撇下的). The 'you' (ta) follows in the third unit, so these participles hang waiting for it. The Ming gives 'the neck', not 'my neck'; the speaker's owning it is my inference from the next unit.

morph.gloss: adjectival locative: that which is on …

sentences.l: Collar-on's cangue wood (acc.), you who had caused-to-be-avoided,
sentences.i: and who turned aside the cangue-wood at the collar,
sentences.n: žaqa-daki is žaqa 'collar' + -deki, 'that on the collar' (Ming 衣領上的). žarbijal 枷 is the cangue, and mudun-i again 'wood (acc.)'. žailaγuluγsan is žaila- 'avoid, dodge' + causative -γul- + -γsan; the Ming 敎躱了的 'made dodge'. The clause says only that the wood was avoided; who wore it is left to the hearer.

sentences.t: ta ečiges köġüd-ün tusa ažuγ̇ui že

morph.gloss: particle: 'indeed' (Ming 也者), a closing emphasis [也者︀]

sentences.l: You, fathers' sons' favour you were, indeed.
sentences.i: were a benefit to fathers and sons, indeed.
sentences.n: ta 'you' (您, plural or polite). ečiges is ečige 'father' + plural -s; köġüd-ün is köġün 'son' + plural -d + genitive -ün, so 'of the sons'. tusa 恩 is 'favour, benefit'. ažuγui is a- 'be' + the past -žuγui, 'was'. že 'indeed' (也者). 'Us fathers and sons' is my reading of the Ming's 父每子每的恩, 'fathers' and sons' favour'; the line may be general and not mean the speaker himself.

sentences.l: You; why were-late you?" he said.
sentences.i: Why were you late?" he said.
sentences.n: jakin 'why' (爲甚); udaba is uda- 'be late' + past -ba (遲了). The second ta repeats the first, giving the question emphasis. keġebe closes the speech.

words.reading: 鎻舌兒中罕-失舌剌 Sorγan-Šira

sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira, saying:
sentences.i: Sorqan-Shira answered:
sentences.n: ügülerün again introduces the reply.

sentences.t: "Bi dotora-γ̇an bölen idgel sedkižü büleġe; jakin jaγ̇araqu bi.

morph.gloss: being present, at hand (Ming 見在; form unclear) [見在]

sentences.l: "I inside-self existing reliance, thinking, was; why hurrying I.
sentences.i: "I had been thinking to rely on what I had within me; why should I hurry?
sentences.n: The reading of this unit is the least secure of the part. dotora-γan is dotora 'inside' + reflexive -γan 'own' (Ming 內自的行). bölen 見在 is 'existing, present'; idgel 倚仗 'reliance'. sedkižü büleġe is sedki- 'think' + -žü, with bü- 'be' in the past, 'I was thinking'. I read 'I had been thinking to rely on what I had in myself (my own position)', but 'in my own mind' is also possible. jaγaraqu is jaγara- 'hurry' + -qu; the Ming 忙 'hurried'.

sentences.t: Jaγ̇aražu urid ireġesü Taičiγ̇ud nojad min-u qočoruγsan eme köġün
sentences.l: Hurrying, first coming-if, Taičiγ̇ud nobles my left-behind wife and son,
sentences.i: If I had hurried and come first, the Taichi'ud lords, my wife and son left behind,
sentences.n: The sentence is a conditional with the verb postponed: jaγaražu urid ireġesü, 'hurrying, first, coming-if'. nojad is nojan 'noble' plural. qočoruγsan (落後的) 'left behind'. The verb comes in the next unit; whether the lords or the wife and son are the subject of keisgekün is not settled by the Ming, and I take the lords as acting.

morph.gloss: food, fodder (Ming 喫食) [喫食 行]
participle in -kün (its force is uncertain; here read as 'would …')

sentences.l: Herd of horses, food (acc.), mine, like ashes would-scatter.
sentences.i: my herds and provisions: they would have scattered them like ashes.
sentences.n: hünesü-ġer is hünesü 'ash' + instrumental -ġer, 'by way of ashes' (灰飛般, 'like ash blown'). keisgekün is keisge- 'scatter, blow away' + -kün, which I take as the participle of what was likely to happen (Ming 廢了, 'ruined'). The same verb keisgen appears again in §148. ideġen-i 喫食行 I read as 'food' (it is not clear whether it is grain, fodder or provisions).

sentences.t: tede keġežü ülü jaγ̇aran edöġe Qaγan-dur(i)-jan neilen idürežü irebe ba" keġebe.

words.reading: 中合中罕-都︀舌里-顏 Qaγan-dur(i)-jan

morph.gloss: to drive on, press on (Ming 趕到) [趕到着]

sentences.l: Those saying, not hurrying, now, Qaγan-with-own joining, driving-on, came, we."
sentences.i: Because they said so I did not hurry; now we have joined our own Qahan, pressing on, and come,"
sentences.n: tede keġežü ülü jaγaran is 'those saying, not hurrying'; the Ming 那的每說着 does not tell whether the words were said to him or about him, so I give 'because they said so' as a loose reading. Qaγan-dur(i)-jan: dative-locative with the reflexive -jan, 'with his own qahan'. neilen is neile- 'join' + -n; idürežü (趕到着) is 'driving on, pressing on'. ba 'we' (exclusive) closes the quotation, then keġebe in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to end, be finished (as an auxiliary: 'when done') [了(呵)]

sentences.l: Speaking finished-when, "Right," said.
sentences.i: When he had spoken, [Chinggis] said, "Good."
sentences.n: kelelen baraγasu: kelele- 'speak' + -n, then bara- 'finish' + conditional -γasu, 'having finished speaking' (Ming 說了呵). žöb is the Ming's 勺(卜), a marked correction of the printed character; I take it as 'right, so be it'. The subject of keġebe is unstated; it is Chinggis.

sentences.l: Again Čiṅgis Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spoke again:
sentences.n: basa 'again' (再) and the usual ügülerün: introducing a speech. §147 is one speech by Chinggis, then Jebe's reply, then Chinggis again.

morph.gloss: to shift position (Ming 相挪; first half of a word split across a line) [相挪]
pressing on, closing up (Ming 趲; second half of the split word; form unclear) [趲]
to put in order, array [相整搠]
reciprocal: one another (Ming 相; the division of this ending is uncertain)

sentences.l: "Köiten, facing-each-other, shifting-hastening, arraying-one-another, being-when,
sentences.i: "When we stood facing one another at Köiten, shifting about and drawing up our ranks,
sentences.n: baildužu is baildu- 'stand facing one another' (Ming 對陣着 'drawn up opposite'). iquri- and γaldun are one phrase cut across the printed line (Ming 相挪 + 趲); I take it as 'shifting about and pressing close'. žibšijelülčen: žibšije- 'put in order' with an ending I split as -lül- + -čen (Ming 相整搠, 'arranging one another'); the reciprocal sense is the Ming's, the division of the ending is my guess. büküi-dür is bü- 'be' + -küi + -dür: 'while being', a time clause. Köiten is Shiratori's spelling of a place name and the Ming says only 地名.

morph.gloss: ridge, spine of a range [嶺脊]
ablative: from (front-vowel form, written with a long ē)

sentences.l: those ridge's from-top, an arrow came.
sentences.i: an arrow came from the top of their ridge
sentences.n: tede nirγun deġerēče: 'those ridge from-top'. deġerēče is deġere 'top' + the ablative -ēče (front-vowel form, written with a long ē). sumun irežü: 'an arrow, coming'. Ming 來着.

sentences.t: min-u žebelekü aman čaγan qula-jin aman-niriġü in-ü quγu ken qarblaγ̇a.

morph.gloss: (with aman) collarbone (Ming 鎖子骨 for the compound)
his, her (genitive stem of the third person) [他的]

sentences.l: My fighting white-mouthed bay's collarbone, its, broken; who shot?
sentences.i: and broke the collarbone of my white-mouthed bay war-horse; who shot it?
sentences.n: žebelekü (戰的) 'for fighting' + aman čaγan qula-jin 'of the white-mouthed bay' is the horse, three words ahead of aman-niriġü 'collarbone' (Ming 鎖子骨). aman 'mouth' appears twice: once as 'white-mouthed' (the muzzle), once in the compound for the bone. in-ü is 'its'. quγu 'broken' (折). ken 'who' qarblaγa: qarbu- 'shoot' plus a verbal -la- and the past -γa. That it is a horse rests on 馬 in the Ming gloss of qula (黃馬).

morph.gloss: ablative: from (front-vowel form, written with a long ē)

sentences.l: From the mountain-top," he said.
sentences.i: From the mountain-top," he said.
sentences.n: Chinggis's answer to his own question, in the same breath. aγula 'mountain' (山); deġerēče as above.

sentences.l: That word-in, Žebe, saying:
sentences.i: At this Jebe spoke:
sentences.n: üge-dür is 'in the word' (Ming 言語裏), 'in that speech'. The man is Žebe, here printed in the conventional form.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (front-vowel form, written with a long ē)

sentences.l: "Mountain's from-top I shot.
sentences.i: "It was I who shot from the mountain-top.
sentences.n: The quotation mark opens at aγula. 'I shot' is bi qarblaγa; no stress is written, but a Mongol subject pronoun is rarely used without emphasis.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to, by (the one acting on the passive verb below)
passive (the form after l): be … (my analysis)

sentences.l: Now, by the Qaγan, put-to-death-if,
sentences.i: Now, if I am put to death by the Qahan,
sentences.n: edöġe 'now'. Qaγan-a is the dative-locative, here the Qahan as the one by whom he would be acted on (the Ming 行). üküġüldeġešü: ükü- 'die' + the causative -ġül- ('make die, kill') + -de-, which I take as the passive after l (the passive is -γda- elsewhere, as in sojurγaγdaγasu two units on) + the conditional -ġešü: 'if one is put to death'. The Ming 皇帝行 敎死呵 fits: 'to/by the Qahan, caused to die, if'. The other reading, 'if I cause the Qahan to die', does not suit the contrast with 'if favoured' two units on; the passive -de- is my analysis and the Ming does not label it.

sentences.l: Palm's so-much earth, rotting, I would-be-left.
sentences.i: I would be left rotting in a patch of earth no bigger than my palm.
sentences.n: halaγan-u tedüi γažar: 'a palm's that-much land', with the house rendering of tedüi after a genitive, 'no bigger than'. höġežü (爛着) 'rotting'; qočorsu (落後我) 'I would be left behind', with the first-person ending -su. The idiom 'left behind as a palm's worth of rotting earth' may be a figure for being put to death; I follow the Ming.

sentences.t: Sojurγaγdaγ̇asu Qaγ̇an-u emüne čeġel usun-i hoγtoru

words.reading: 莎余舌兒中合黑荅阿速 Sojurγaγdaγ̇asu

glyphs.s: 莎余舌兒中合黑荅阿速

sentences.l: Favoured-if, Qaγan's in front, deep water (acc.) cutting-across,
sentences.i: But if I am shown favour — before the Qahan, cutting across deep water,
sentences.n: sojurγaγdaγasu is sojurγa- 'show favour' (Ming 恩賜) + passive -γda- + conditional -γasu: 'if favoured'. Qaγan-u emüne: 'Qahan's front' (前行). čeġel usun-i 'deep water' and hoγtoru 'cutting across' (橫斷). The unit goes on in the next.

morph.gloss: first-person optative (Ming 與我): I will …

sentences.l: clear stones smashing, charging, I will give.
sentences.i: smashing the bright stones, charging, I will give.
sentences.n: čegen čilaγun čaγuru is 'clear stone smashing' (明石碎): čaγuru is a converb 'smashing'. dobtulžu 衝着 'charging'. ögsü: ög- 'give' with the first-person -sü (Ming 與我, 'I give'). What is given is not stated; the Ming says only 'I give'.

sentences.l: Reach having-said place-to,
sentences.i: To the place to which you say 'Reach',
sentences.n: kür is the bare stem of kür- 'reach, arrive' (Ming 到). keġegsen γažar-a: 'said place-to' (說的地行). I take the 'you' to be Chinggis, though the Mongol does not say.

morph.gloss: (Ming 惹) an unresolved word, perhaps a command or particle [惹]

sentences.l: Blue stone smash 'qal' said-when,
sentences.i: and when you say 'smash the blue stone'
sentences.n: kökö gürü keġürü: 'blue stone smash' (靑石碎). qal glosses 惹, which I cannot place; it might be an imperative particle. keġegsen-dür: 'when said' (-dür again as a time marker). The sense of this and the previous unit is that he will go where he is told and strike what he is told.

sentences.t: qara gürü qamqaru dobtulžu ögsü" keġebe.

morph.gloss: first-person optative (Ming 與我): I will …

sentences.l: black stone smashing, charging, I will give." he said.
sentences.i: smashing the black stone too, charging, I will give," he said.
sentences.n: qara gürü qamqaru dobtulžu ögsü: 'black stone smashing, charging, I will give' repeats the pattern of the blue-stone clause and answers it: the two-line vow pairs bright/blue stones with black stone. The stones are probably a figure of what he will break through; the Ming gives no more.

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Same formula; now Chinggis answers Jebe's vow.

morph.gloss: to kill [殺︀了的 自的行]

words.reading: 歹亦速舌兒中合黑撒你-顏 daisurγaγsan(i)-jan

glyphs.s: 歹亦速舌兒中合黑撒你-顏

morph.gloss: to turn enemy, rebel [反做了的 自的行]

sentences.l: "An enemy gone man, his killing, his enemy-making,
sentences.i: "A man who has gone as an enemy — his killing, his turning hostile —
sentences.n: daisun jabuγsan küġün: 'enemy-gone person' (敵行了的人), a participle phrase. alaγsan(i)-jan and daisurγaγsan(i)-jan are two participles with an accusative (i) and the reflexive-possessive -jan, 'his own killing', 'his own enemy-making' (Ming 自的行). The two nouns are objects of the fear in the next unit.

morph.gloss: to hide (printed miγu-, but the Ming character 你 reads ni-) [藏着]

sentences.l: his body hiding, his speech concealing, fears.
sentences.i: hides himself, conceals his words and is afraid.
sentences.n: beje-ġen 'his own body' (身自的), kele-ben 'his own speech' (話自的): the reflexive possessive again, this time with -ġen and -ben (two shapes of the same ending, both after a vowel stem here; I cannot say what chooses between them). miγužu is printed with m but the Ming 你 reads ni; I take it as niγu- 'hide'. bučažu 'concealing' (諱着). aju: aju- 'fear' (怕有).

morph.gloss: converb: being; after a pronoun, 'as for'
on the contrary, rather (Ming 卻) [卻]

sentences.l: This one, as for, if one says, on the contrary,
sentences.i: But this man, if I speak of him:
sentences.n: bürün is bü- 'to be' with the converb -rün, which after a pronoun gives 'as for' (Ming 呵), as in earlier parts. kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + the conditional -sü, 'if one says'. munda is the Ming's 卻 'on the contrary'.

sentences.t: alaγsan(i)-jan daisurγaγsan(i)-jan ülü buča munda žiγ̇an bijü;

morph.gloss: to kill [殺︀了的 自的行]

words.reading: 歹亦速舌兒中合黑撒你-顏 daisurγaγsan(i)-jan

glyphs.s: 歹亦速舌兒中合黑撒你-顏

morph.gloss: to turn enemy, rebel [反做了的 自的行]
to conceal (bare stem, used as a finite verb) [隱諱]
on the contrary, rather (Ming 卻) [卻]
converb used as a finite verb: is

sentences.l: his killing, his enemy-making, not concealed, on the contrary tells.
sentences.i: he has not hidden what he killed or his rebelling, but tells them,
sentences.n: the same two participles, this time with ülü buča: ülü 'not', buča 'conceal' (bare stem, as a finite verb). munda žiγan: 'on the contrary, telling'. bijü 'is'. Shiratori puts a semicolon after bijü.

morph.gloss: converb used as a finite verb: is

sentences.l: Companion-having person is."
sentences.i: he is a man fit to be a companion."
sentences.n: nököčeltü is nököčel 'companionship' + -tü, 'companion-having', the possessive pattern (Ming 可做伴的 'fit to be a companion'). Shiratori closes the quotation after bijü.

sentences.l: Žirγoγ̇adai name-having was.
sentences.i: His name had been Jirgo'adai.
sentences.n: Narration after the speech. neretü is nere 'name' + -tü; ažuγu is the past of a- 'be', as ažuγui earlier. This tells us that Jebe was first called Jirgo'adai; the next units give the reason for the new name.

sentences.t: Mün žebelekü aman čaγan qula-ji min-u aman-niruγ̇u qarbuγsan-u tula

morph.gloss: the very, the same (Ming 只/他) [他]
(with aman) collarbone (Ming 鎖子骨 for the compound)

words.reading: 中合舌兒鏷黑撒訥 qarbuγsan-u

morph.gloss: because of, on account of [上頭]

sentences.l: That very fighting white-mouthed bay (acc.), my collarbone, of the shooting, because-of,
sentences.i: Because he had shot the collarbone of that very white-mouthed bay war-horse of mine,
sentences.n: mün 'the very' as in the Ming 他. qula-ji: accusative of qula 'bay horse'. aman-niruγu 'collarbone' (spelled -niruγu here and -niriġü above); the same compound. qarbuγsan-u tula is 'of the shooting, because-of': a participle in the genitive plus tula 上頭 'on account of'.

morph.gloss: him, that one (Ming 敎他; form unclear) [敎他]

sentences.l: Žebe name-taking, let-us-fight, him, saying,
sentences.i: he said, 'Taking the name Jebe, let us set him to fight',
sentences.n: nereidčü is nere 'name' + -id- 'take as a name' + -čü (Ming 名字做着). žebeleje is žebele- 'fight' + the hortative -je, the Ming 戰咱 'let us fight'. The name Žebe and the verb žebele- look related; I only note it. ima-ji 敎他 is 'him' (the Ming 'cause him'); I could not analyse ima. Ming: 'let us make him fight'.

sentences.t: Žebe nereidčü dergede min-u jabu" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Žebe name-taking, in-presence my go, saying, decree made.
sentences.i: 'Taking the name Jebe, go at my side,' he said, and made it a decree.
sentences.n: dergede 根前 is 'in front of, in the presence of'. jabu is the bare stem of jabu- 'go', here a command (Ming 行). žarliγ bolba 'a decree was made' (聖旨做了), as in §145. So the new name came with the order to ride at his side.

sentences.t: Žebe Taičiγ̇ud-ača irežü nököčegsen josun teimü.

morph.gloss: to be a companion [做伴來的]

sentences.l: Žebe, from the Taičiγ̇ud, coming, companion-being reason, thus.
sentences.i: That was the reason Jebe came from the Taichi'ud and became his companion.
sentences.n: Taičiγud-ača is the ablative 'from the Taichi'ud'. irežü 'coming'. nököčegsen josun teimü: 'the reason of having been a companion, thus' (Ming 做伴來的理那般). josun 理 is 'reason, rightness'. This is Shiratori's closing summary, ending the section.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people [種(名) 行]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, there, Taičiγ̇ud (acc.), plundering,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan plundered the Taichi'ud there,
sentences.n: tende 'there' (那裏). Taičiγud-i is the people with the accusative. daγuližu is daγuli- (擄着), a converb 'plundering, seizing'. The sentence continues over the next two units.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇utai jasutu küġün-i Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur, Qoton-Orčaṅ, Quduγ̇udar-tan

words.reading: 阿兀出-把阿禿舌兒 Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur

morph.gloss: A'uchu, a man's name [人名 勇士]

words.reading: 中忽都︀兀荅舌兒-壇 Quduγ̇udar-tan

sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud-with bone-having persons (acc.), Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur, Qoton-Orčaṅ, Quduγ̇udar and others,
sentences.i: taking those of noble bone among the Taichi'ud, A'uchu-Ba'atur, Qotun-Orchang, Qudu'udar and the others,
sentences.n: jasutu is jasu(n) 'bone' + -tü, 'bone-having', the possessive pattern; the Ming 骨頭有的 is the same literal phrase. I take it as 'of noble bone', a lineage term, but that is an inference. Taičiγutai: the Ming 種(名) says only 'people name'; the -tai may be 'with, having'. -tan after Qudu'udar is the plural-collective 'and the like' (人名等). The three names are given in apposition to küġün-i.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud-i Uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele hünesü-ġer keisgen kiduba.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people [種(名)每 行]

sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud (acc.), descendant's descendant-to until, like ashes scattering, killed-off.
sentences.i: He killed off the Taichi'ud, down to their children's children, scattering them like ashes.
sentences.n: Uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele: 'of descendant, to descendant, until' (Ming 子孫的子孫行直到). hünesü-ġer keisgen: 'by-way-of-ashes, scattering' (灰飛般颺), the same image as in §146. kiduba: kidu- 'kill off' (盡殺了) + past.

morph.gloss: their (genitive stem of the third person) [他的]

sentences.l: Nation, people (acc.), their, causing-to-move, coming.
sentences.i: He set their nation and people in motion and came.
sentences.n: Ulus irgen-i: 'nation, people (acc.)'; an-u 'their' (his) is the genitive stem of the third person; ködölgežü is ködöl- 'move' + causative -ge- + -žü (敎動着). irežü 'coming'.

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, Qubaqaja, wintered.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan wintered at Qubaqaja.
sentences.n: übülžebe is übül 'winter' + a verb-forming -že- + past -be (住冬了). Qubaqaja is a place name (Ming 地名).
